6403.title: Performance Testing
6403.heading: Performance Testing
6403.content:
Performance testing measures how an application behaves under a defined workload. Response time, throughput, and failures provide a baseline that can be compared after a query, controller, cache, or hosting change.

The measurement must keep workload and environment comparable. Without a baseline, a faster-looking implementation may simply have been tested under different conditions or may have shifted its cost elsewhere.

The const declaration prevents modification of configured parameters while allowing explicitly mutable working state. The hook commonly delegates to initialization and iteration helpers rather than becoming one monolithic function.

6409.sourceSearchName: perfect square trinomial perfect square trinomial
6409.title: Perfect Square Trinomial
6409.heading: Perfect Square Trinomial
6409.content:
A perfect square trinomial is a three-term polynomial that is the square of a binomial:

$$a^2+2ab+b^2=(a+b)^2,$$

or

$$a^2-2ab+b^2=(a-b)^2.$$

Its first and last terms are squares, and its middle term is twice the product of their square roots with the appropriate sign. Recognizing this structure permits immediate factorization. [[Completing the Square]] creates the structure when the original quadratic lacks the needed constant term.

6412.title: Perception
6412.heading: Perception
6412.content:
Perception gives sensed stimuli a meaningful interpretation. It is the first major stage of [[Information Processing]] and supplies the information that [[Cognition]] uses to choose actions.

A [[3D User Interface]] can communicate through visual, auditory, haptic, chemical, and vestibular channels. Each channel has different strengths, limits, and cues. Designers need to understand these mechanisms because display choices can strengthen, omit, or conflict with the information people normally use in a physical environment.

Perceptual evaluation can combine observation, performance measures, self-report, and methods such as eye tracking.

6415.title: Perceptron
6415.heading: Perceptron
6415.content:
A Perceptron is an [[Artificial Neuron]] whose activation is a step function. It outputs one when its weighted input and bias cross the threshold and zero otherwise.

A single Perceptron can learn a linear [[Decision Boundary]] and separate two classes when the observations are linearly separable. More complicated boundaries require networks that combine multiple neurons in connected layers.

In the book's classification treatment, a perceptron has input nodes fully connected to class outputs, combines inputs through weights, and applies an activation function. Its learning rule can find a linear separator when one exists; the XOR example demonstrates why nonlinear problems require hidden layers and a multilayer network.

Kelleher describes Rosenblatt's rule as error correction after each labeled example: if the output is correct the weights remain unchanged; otherwise, weights are changed in a direction intended to correct the mistake. The [[Learning Rate]] scales those changes. The convergence result applies when a separating set of weights exists, but an unsuccessful long run alone cannot tell whether convergence is merely slow or impossible for the examples.

6418.title: Percentile
6418.heading: Percentile
6418.content:
A percentile is a value below which a specified percentage of ordered observations falls. The 50th percentile is the median, while the 25th and 75th percentiles bound the central half of a distribution.

Percentiles describe position without assuming a normal distribution and help identify plausible ranges or recoding cutpoints. Their sample estimates can repeat when measurements are discrete or capped, so several requested percentiles may share the same observed value.

6421.title: Perceived Difficulty
6421.heading: Perceived Difficulty
6421.content:
Perceived difficulty is how hard a challenge feels to a particular player. It combines intrinsic skill, stress, power supplied by the game, and the player's in-game experience with similar challenges.

Because native talent and prior gaming experience also differ, designers cannot predict perception exactly. Difficulty modes, gradual teaching, observation, and testing with representative players help manage the range.

6424.title: Penetration Testing
6424.heading: Penetration Testing
6424.content:
Penetration testing deliberately attempts to circumvent a system's protections and gain unauthorized logical access. It is used to find security gaps before an uncontrolled attacker exploits them.

Cloud services can schedule penetration tests as part of proactive monitoring and assurance, subject to the provider's rules and the system's scope. Findings should lead to remediation and retesting rather than serving only as a one-time report.

Penetration testing belongs throughout a [[Secure Software Development Lifecycle]] rather than only after construction. Used alongside [[Security Code Review]] and [[Security Architecture Analysis]], it can reveal exploitable behavior early enough to change the design as well as the deployment.
links: Layered Cyber Defense and Secure Development

6427.title: Peltier Effect
6427.heading: Peltier Effect
6427.content: The Peltier effect exchanges heat at the junction of two materials when electrical current crosses it. Reversing current reverses whether that junction releases or absorbs heat, making it a reversible thermoelectric effect. Its heat rate is proportional to current through the Peltier coefficient. In a [[Thermoelectric Generator]], this heat exchange belongs in the hot- and cold-junction energy balances.

6430.title: Peer-to-Peer Game Topology
6430.heading: Peer-to-Peer Game Topology
6430.content:
A peer-to-peer game topology has participating machines exchange state or commands without one separate authoritative server. Real-time strategy games can use this model by sending player commands while each peer runs the same deterministic simulation.

The approach reduces centralized hosting needs but makes synchronization, late joining, disconnection, trust, and cheating harder. A slow or divergent peer can affect the entire shared session.

6433.title: Pearson Chi-Squared Test
6433.heading: Pearson Chi-Squared Test
6433.content:
The Pearson chi-squared test compares observed cell counts in a [[Contingency Table]] with the counts expected if its categorical variables were independent. Its statistic increases as observed counts depart from those expectations.

The p-value is evaluated with degrees of freedom determined by the table dimensions. Sparse expected cells can undermine the approximation, in which case a [[Fisher Exact Test]] may be more appropriate.

6436.title: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
6436.heading: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
6436.content:
The Pearson correlation coefficient measures the direction and strength of a linear relationship between two quantitative variables. It ranges from -1 to 1, with zero indicating no linear association.

The coefficient is sensitive to outliers and can be small when a strong relationship is nonlinear. A p-value may test whether the population correlation differs from zero, but a large sample can make a weak, practically unimportant coefficient statistically significant.

The source further warns that correlation measures linear association, not agreement or reproducibility. Its compact interpretation is most complete for approximately bivariate-normal data; shared trends, broad ranges, or a single extreme observation can otherwise create a misleadingly high value.

6442.title: Payback Period
6442.heading: Payback Period
6442.content:
The payback period is the time required for the benefits of an investment to recover its cost. If a service produces a measurable monthly gain, the accumulated gain can be compared with the committed service cost to estimate when the investment pays for itself.

Shorter payback is attractive, but the method ignores the changing value of money over time and benefits that arrive after the cutoff. [[Net Present Value]] adds a discount rate when timing materially affects the decision.

6445.sourceSearchName: pay to win pay to win
6445.title: Pay-to-Win
6445.heading: Pay-to-Win
6445.content:
Pay-to-win is a monetization design in which spending real money provides a competitive gameplay advantage unavailable on equal terms to nonpaying players. Wealth outside the game changes the effective rules of competition.

The source treats this as a violation of fair multiplayer play. Asymmetric roles can still be fair, but a purchased advantage produces an arms race based on spending rather than skill or decisions.

6448.title: Pattern-Space Clustering
6448.heading: Pattern-Space Clustering
6448.content:
Pattern-space clustering groups data objects using their mapped relationships to selected patterns. Objects can be similar because they share structural motifs even when their original encodings differ greatly.

Pattern features can also define subspaces associated with distinct clusters. Redundant ubiquitous patterns should be controlled so that meaningful structural variation dominates the distance measure.

6451.heading: Pattern-Defined Sequence Feature
6451.content:
A pattern-defined sequence feature combines a sequence pattern with a usage method. The pattern states what ordered structure to recognize, while the usage method turns its matches into a value or set of values.

Separating these two parts clarifies that one mined pattern can support several representations. Presence, frequency, interval counts, positions, and sliding-window summaries emphasize different aspects of the same matches.

6454.title: Pattern-Based Feature Generation
6454.heading: Pattern-Based Feature Generation
6454.content:
Pattern-based feature generation discovers structured patterns in data and converts them into dimensions for analysis or learning. The workflow separates pattern mining, pattern selection, and pattern-to-value mapping.

This separation makes the representation explicit: mining defines the candidate vocabulary, selection controls quality and size, and mapping determines how each data object is encoded.

6457.title: Pattern Space
6457.heading: Pattern Space
6457.content:
A pattern space is the set of structured patterns permitted by a representation and its constraints. Itemsets, sequences, subgraphs, and other pattern families create different spaces with different matching rules.

The space is usually enormous, so support thresholds, structural restrictions, and task-specific bounds determine which candidates can be enumerated. Its definition limits both expressiveness and computational cost.

6459.sourceSearchName: pattern selection phase pattern selection phase
6459.title: Pattern Selection Phase
6459.heading: Document

6460.sourceSearchName: pattern selection phase pattern selection phase
6460.title: Pattern Selection Phase
6460.heading: Pattern Selection Phase
6460.content:
The pattern selection phase chooses a manageable, informative subset from mined candidates. Criteria can measure redundancy, coverage, discrimination, stability, or downstream performance.

Selection prevents the representation from inheriting the full combinatorial output of mining. Post-processing evaluates an existing candidate set, while in-process methods prune during enumeration.

6463.title: Pattern Recognition
6463.heading: Pattern Recognition
6463.content:
Pattern recognition infers a hidden category or structure from observed features. A probabilistic description models how each candidate pattern could generate the available evidence and uses prior knowledge to resolve ambiguous matches.

Classification is one common question posed to such a model. Marginalizing nuisance variables permits recognition to tolerate variations that are not part of the desired category.

6466.sourceSearchName: pattern post processing pruning pattern post processing pruning
6466.title: Pattern Post-Processing Pruning
6466.heading: Pattern Post-Processing Pruning
6466.content:
Pattern post-processing pruning removes redundant or low-value patterns after mining has produced a candidate collection. It can use equivalence, subsumption, correlation, coverage, or model performance.

Because the full candidates already exist, post-processing is flexible but may inherit the mining phase's memory cost. Earlier constraint pushing is preferable when the raw pattern set is too large to materialize.

6469.heading: Pattern Mining Phase
6469.content:
The pattern mining phase searches the pattern space for candidates satisfying constraints such as minimum support or class contrast. It produces the raw vocabulary from which pattern features may be constructed.

Mining is distinct from choosing the final model inputs. A frequent candidate can be redundant or nonpredictive, so later selection or in-process pruning remains necessary.

6472.content:
A pattern mapping function converts the relationship between an object and a pattern into a feature value. Common mappings encode binary match, frequency, confidence, or class growth behavior.

The same pattern set can yield different learning spaces under different mappings. A mapping should reflect what match strength means for the data type and task.

Pattern consequence analysis records both the flexibility a design pattern creates and the costs it introduces. Visitor makes new tree operations easy but new node types difficult; Strategy supports replacement but adds indirection and compatibility checks.

The analysis keeps a pattern from being adopted as decoration. A useful design chooses a consequence profile that matches the changes expected in the clustering library.

6487.title: Pathfinding Graph
6487.heading: Pathfinding Graph
6487.content:
A pathfinding graph represents traversable space as nodes connected by edges. Nodes stand for locations or regions, edges represent allowed movement, and edge costs estimate the expense of traveling between them.

A grid, collection of [[Path Node|path nodes]], or [[Navigation Mesh]] can all produce a graph searched by the same general algorithm. Representation determines route quality, memory use, and search cost.

6489.sourceSearchName: passive navigation receiver passive navigation receiver
6489.title: Passive Navigation Receiver
6489.heading: Document

6490.sourceSearchName: passive navigation receiver passive navigation receiver
6490.title: Passive Navigation Receiver
6490.heading: Passive Navigation Receiver
6490.content: A passive navigation receiver listens to external signals but does not transmit in order to obtain a fix. LORAN, Omega, Transit, and GPS all used this property, which lets many users share a service without consuming return-channel capacity or disclosing their positions to the navigation provider. Passivity improves scalability and operational security, although a receiver still depends on the availability and authenticity of the signals it observes.

6491.sourceSearchName: passive navigation receiver passive navigation receiver
6491.title: Passive Navigation Receiver
6491.heading: References

6493.title: Passive Challenge
6493.heading: Passive Challenge
6493.content:
A passive challenge is created by a static obstacle or spatial arrangement that does not require additional mechanics to operate. A maze can challenge navigation even when its walls never change.

Passive does not mean trivial. Layout, visibility, memory demand, and route structure can produce substantial difficulty without an adversary or continuously executing process.

6496.title: Path Node
6496.heading: Path Node
6496.content:
A path node is a deliberately placed location used as a vertex in a [[Pathfinding Graph]]. Connections between visible or reachable nodes define the routes an agent may consider.

Path-node networks can be compact but require careful authoring and may constrain movement to conspicuous corridors. A [[Navigation Mesh]] instead represents connected walkable regions and usually permits more natural choices within each region.

6499.title: Password Authentication
6499.heading: Password Authentication
6499.content:
Password authentication verifies a claimed identity through a secret the user knows. Its security depends on both the quality of the secret and the way the system stores, transmits, verifies, and recovers it.

Passwords are vulnerable to guessing, reuse, theft, and deceptive collection. A [[Cryptographic Salt]] and hash can improve stored-password protection, while [[Multi-Factor Authentication]] reduces dependence on the password as the only evidence of identity.

6502.sourceSearchName: party based interaction model party based interaction model
6502.title: Party-Based Interaction Model
6502.heading: Party-Based Interaction Model
6502.content:
A party-based interaction model gives the player control over a small group of characters that usually remain together but may separate briefly. It is common in role-playing games.

The interface must make selection, orders, inventory, formation, and individual status manageable without losing the group as a coherent unit. Aerial views and point-and-click navigation often support this scope.

6503.title: Party-Based Interaction Model

6505.title: Party Switching
6505.heading: Party Switching
6505.content:
Party switching occurs when a legislator leaves an original political group for another or joins a newly created group. The decision may reflect career strategy, institutional bargaining, party weakness, or changing alliances.

Temporal community analysis can reveal a lawmaker's network position moving between groups before or alongside an official switch. The inference requires repeated snapshots because an aggregate term-wide graph hides the transition.

6508.title: Party Discipline
6508.heading: Party Discipline
6508.content:
Party discipline is the consistency with which legislators remain aligned with their political organization. In a network, persistent within-party relationships and the absence of member departures can provide evidence of cohesion.

Discipline is shaped by institutional incentives and cannot be inferred from one aggregate graph alone. Session-level community patterns help distinguish stable alignment from temporary cross-party collaboration.

6511.title: Party Splitting
6511.heading: Party Splitting
6511.content:
Party splitting occurs when one political organization divides into separate parliamentary groups. It is a group-level change that can happen while individual legislators are also [[Party Switching|switching parties]].

Official group counts and co-sponsorship communities need not divide in the same way. Dense collaboration may persist across formal splits, making session-level networks necessary to compare institutional labels with behavior.

The remedy is to select thinner slices that combine design, code, art, audio, and testing into playable value each Sprint. Integration then becomes a source of continuing knowledge rather than an end-stage crisis.

6517.title: Partitioned Matrix
6517.heading: Partitioned Matrix
6517.content:
A partitioned matrix divides a larger array into rectangular submatrices. The blocks behave as matrix-valued entries, provided their dimensions remain compatible with the operation being performed.

Finite element systems naturally acquire block structure when degrees of freedom are grouped by node, component, or prescribed versus free values. Partitioning exposes those groups so boundary conditions and subsystem equations can be handled without rewriting every scalar entry.

6520.heading: Partitional Clustering Container
6520.content:
PClustering is a container of shared Cluster pointers representing one flat partition. It can remove empty clusters, assign cluster identifiers, save assigned records, calculate cluster sizes, and compare memberships with any labels supplied in the dataset.

Storing base pointers lets the same partition contain derived center or subspace clusters. Calculated summaries should be invalidated when membership changes so output does not mix current clusters with stale counts.

6523.title: Partition Clustering
6523.heading: Partition Clustering
6523.content:
Partition clustering produces one division of the data rather than a complete nested hierarchy. It usually optimizes an objective over all observations or repeatedly improves a current assignment.

Partition methods are attractive when constructing a full dendrogram is too expensive. Their main challenges are choosing the number of clusters, selecting an initial configuration, and avoiding poor local optima.

A partition index vector records which rows belong to training, validation, or test subsets. Saving the indices makes the split auditable and permits identical partitions across competing models.

Indices should remain aligned with stable record identifiers so row reordering cannot silently change membership.

This correspondence explains why quotient constructions organize elements into nonoverlapping classes.

A partition summary calculates cluster counts and sizes and, when labels are present, builds a cross-tabulation between discovered cluster indexes and supplied classes. The table reveals how each unlabeled group overlaps known categories.

Cluster indexes have no inherent correspondence with class labels, so the table is more informative than comparing index numbers directly. It remains an external diagnostic, not a parameter used by the unsupervised algorithm.

6541.heading: Particle Interactions and Behaviors
6541.content: A simple particle may move according to emission and forces without considering its neighbors. A behavioral particle system can additionally use collision, self-interaction, attraction, avoidance, deflection, or crowding to produce organized motion such as a flock or swarm. The extra relationships matter when the effect depends on elements affecting one another rather than merely passing through space. The book treats these as controls layered on top of basic [[Particle Motion Forces and Lifetime]], not as a replacement for emitter timing or rendering choices.

6544.title: Particle Filter
6544.heading: Particle Filter
6544.content:
A particle filter approximates a changing probability distribution with weighted samples. Particles are propagated through the transition model and reweighted by how well their predicted states explain each new observation.

Resampling concentrates computational effort on plausible regions of the state space. This makes nonlinear or non-Gaussian recursive estimation possible when an exact analytic update is impractical.

6547.heading: Particle Emitter Birth and Limit
6547.content: An emitter defines where particles begin, how quickly they are born, and the total number that may exist. A birth rate of one per frame spreads a fixed limit across time; a birth rate equal to the limit releases the whole burst on one frame. That difference helps distinguish a continuous fountain from an explosion. A nozzle determines the initial arrangement, while generation can be triggered by time, keyframe, or an event such as a collision. Later appearance depends on [[Particle Motion Forces and Lifetime]].

Protecting the middle prevents a group from jumping directly from the loudest idea to a solution. Tools such as [[Affinity Mapping]] and root-cause analysis help the group move through ambiguity constructively.

Each action affects both future rewards and the information available through later observations. A policy maps beliefs to actions, coupling recursive state estimation with sequential decision-making.

6559.title: Partial Pivoting
6559.heading: Partial Pivoting
6559.content:
Partial pivoting selects the largest available absolute entry in the current column as the next pivot and interchanges rows to place it in the pivot position.

Used with [[Gaussian Elimination]], it avoids division by a zero pivot and usually limits numerical error. The row exchanges can be recorded by a [[Permutation Matrix]].

6562.title: Partial Fraction Decomposition
6562.heading: Partial Fraction Decomposition
6562.content: Partial fraction decomposition rewrites a [[Proper Rational Function]] as a sum of simpler rational terms determined by the denominator's linear and irreducible quadratic factors. Repeated factors require a term for each power. Multiplying by the common denominator and matching coefficients determines the unknown numerators, preparing the expression for later integration and other operations.

6565.title: Partial Derivative
6565.heading: Partial Derivative
6565.content:
A partial derivative measures how a function of several variables changes with respect to one variable while the others are held constant. It isolates the local effect of that variable on the output.

For a neural network, the variables include its many weights and biases and the output of interest is the [[Loss Function|loss]]. Collecting the partial derivatives for all parameters produces the [[Gradient]].

Second partial derivatives describe how these first-order rates change. Arranging every second and mixed partial derivative into a square array produces the [[Hessian Matrix]], which supports curvature tests and Newton-type optimization.

6568.title: Parser Overgeneration
6568.heading: Parser Overgeneration
6568.content:
Parser overgeneration occurs when a grammar or robust parser accepts inputs outside the intended language and assigns them plausible-looking structures. Permissive rules that improve coverage can therefore increase false interpretations.

The risk is especially high when [[Robust Parsing]] skips unmatched material. Confidence scoring, domain constraints, and confirmation through a [[Clarification Question]] can limit the consequences.

A parking lot data center combines the onboard computers and storage of parked vehicles into a temporary computing facility. Long-term parking provides more stable membership than moving traffic, and physical spaces can supply power and wired networking.

The design must predict departures, isolate owners' systems, coordinate workloads, and offer incentives worth the use of vehicle resources.

6574.title: Parse Tree
6574.heading: Parse Tree
6574.content:
A parse tree displays how a [[Context-Free Grammar]] generates a string. The start symbol is the root, production applications form branches, and terminal symbols read from left to right along the leaves form the generated string.

The tree records grammatical structure without recording the order in which independent productions were applied. Each parse tree corresponds to one left derivation, so a string with two distinct parse trees demonstrates an [[Ambiguous Grammar]].

6577.title: Parkerian Hexad
6577.heading: Parkerian Hexad
6577.content:
The Parkerian hexad expands the [[CIA Triad]] into six information-security properties: [[Information Confidentiality]], [[Information Possession and Control]], [[Data Integrity]], [[Information Authenticity]], [[Information Availability]], and [[Information Utility]].

The properties are intended to expose non-overlapping ways in which information can fail its intended user. For example, correct and confidential data can still be unusable, unavailable, held by an unauthorized party, or falsely attributed to an untrustworthy origin.

6583.title: Parametric Survival Model
6583.heading: Parametric Survival Model
6583.content:
A parametric survival model assumes that event times follow a specified distribution, such as exponential, log-normal, Weibull, gamma, or log-logistic. The distribution supplies a complete mathematical form for survival and hazard over time.

This structure can yield efficient, interpretable estimates when the assumption is credible, but different distributions can reverse conclusions when the fit is poor. Fitted curves and information criteria should guide [[Survival Model Distribution Selection]].

6584.title: Parametric Survival Model
6584.heading: References

6586.title: Parametric Simulation
6586.heading: Parametric Simulation
6586.content:
A parametric simulation generates artificial observations from a chosen probability distribution using specified or estimated parameters. It replaces unavailable population data with a model of the data-generating process.

The source uses estimated means and standard deviations with a normal model to study test behavior. The simulation can evaluate finite-sample approximations, but its conclusions remain conditional on the selected parametric family and parameter values.

6589.title: Parametric Form
6589.heading: Parametric Form
6589.content:
A parametric form specifies how one probability factor in a Bayesian decomposition can be computed from a known family and a set of parameters. Tables, deterministic relationships, and named probability families are examples of forms used by the book.

A factor can also take the form of a question to another Bayesian program. The selected form determines which parameters must be supplied or identified and which inference operations remain feasible.

6592.title: Parametric Distribution
6592.heading: Parametric Distribution
6592.content:
A parametric distribution belongs to a chosen mathematical family whose behavior is determined by a finite set of parameters. A normal family, for example, is specified by parameters controlling its location and spread.

Selecting the family and parameter meanings is preliminary modeling knowledge. Identification then supplies or learns parameter values from data, allowing the distribution to be computed without storing an unrestricted table over every possible case.

6595.title: Parameterized SQL
6595.heading: Parameterized SQL
6595.content:
Parameterized SQL keeps variable values separate from the SQL command text. Dapper binds values from an object to named parameters, allowing the database driver to treat them as data rather than executable query fragments.

This is the normal way to pass identifiers, filters, and inserted values into repository queries. It also makes the intended inputs explicit at the point where a command is executed.

6598.title: Parallelogram Law
6598.heading: Parallelogram Law
6598.content:
The parallelogram law states

$$\|u+v\|^2+\|u-v\|^2=2\|u\|^2+2\|v\|^2.$$

The vectors $u+v$ and $u-v$ form the diagonals of the parallelogram determined by $u$ and $v$. Expanding both squared lengths with the [[Dot Product]] proves the identity by cancellation of the mixed terms.

6601.title: Parameter Prior
6601.heading: Parameter Prior
6601.content:
A parameter prior represents knowledge about model parameters before the selected observations are incorporated. It can favor plausible ranges, express symmetry, or regularize identification when data is limited.

Bayesian estimation multiplies this prior by the data likelihood and normalizes the result. As evidence accumulates, its influence usually becomes smaller unless the observations are weak or ambiguous.

6604.title: Parallelogram Theorems
6604.heading: Parallelogram Theorems
6604.content: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal, opposite angles are equal, adjacent angles are supplementary, and the diagonals bisect one another. A diagonal separates the figure into congruent triangles, allowing these properties to be proved from parallel-line angle relations and [[Triangle Congruence]]. Converse tests use the same properties to establish that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

6607.heading: Parallel-Plate Capacitor
6607.content: An ideal parallel-plate capacitor consists of conducting plates of area $A$ separated by distance $d$. Ignoring edge effects, its capacitance is $C=\varepsilon A/d$, and the field between the plates is approximately uniform with $E=V/d$. Increasing plate area or permittivity raises capacitance; increasing separation lowers it.

6613.heading: Parallel Nested Transaction
6613.content:
A parallel nested transaction runs independent or compatible inner transactions concurrently within one parent operation. The scheduler must preserve the nesting semantics while exposing enough internal structure to assign inner work to different workers.

Parallel nesting can shorten a complex transaction, but hidden dependencies may turn apparent concurrency into repeated aborts or serialization.

6616.title: Parallel LINQ
6616.heading: Parallel LINQ
6616.content:
Parallel LINQ can partition an in-memory query across multiple workers by converting the source with `AsParallel`. It is intended for CPU-bound operations whose independent elements are expensive enough to outweigh partitioning and coordination overhead.

Parallel execution can change ordering and exposes unsafe shared state in query delegates. It should be adopted after measurement, with explicit ordering only when needed and with cancellation and exception behavior accounted for.

The design-patterns source places Parallel LINQ beside concurrent collections and task-based code. The comparison matters: PLINQ partitions a data query for CPU work, whereas `async`/`await` avoids tying up a thread while an operation waits. Applying both labels to a workload does not automatically improve its throughput.

A parallel level layout offers several routes moving toward the same broad destination, with opportunities to switch between them. It resembles a rail yard rather than a single track.

The structure preserves directional progression while adding tactical and exploratory choice. Routes should present meaningful differences rather than cosmetic variations that immediately produce the same experience.

6622.heading: Parallel Fan-Out and Join
6622.content:
A fan-out-and-join computation distributes independent pieces of work to many workers or processors and later combines their results. Fan-out creates parallel activity; join waits for the required outputs and assembles them into the next stage.

The pattern can reduce elapsed time when work is sufficiently independent. Its benefits are limited by uneven task sizes, communication overhead, shared resources, and the need to validate results before joining them.

Clusters often form around separate areas of knowledge; sparse connections between those clusters can become early evidence for a [[Context Map]]. 6631.heading: Parallel Density-Based Clustering
6631.content:
Parallel density-based clustering partitions data or space among workers, performs local neighborhood analysis, and reconciles clusters that cross partition boundaries. Boundary communication is essential because density connectivity can extend through chains held on different machines.

A balanced partition reduces runtime, but skewed densities can overload a worker and generate extensive merging traffic. Correctness requires preserving cross-partition neighbors rather than treating local clusters as independent final results.

6634.title: Parallel Computation
6634.heading: Parallel Computation
6634.content:
Parallel computation divides work so that multiple processors or workers execute parts at the same time. Useful decomposition exposes operations that can proceed independently and defines how their intermediate results will be joined.

Speedup is limited by sequential dependencies, communication, synchronization, and uneven workloads. The architecture and algorithm must therefore be designed together rather than assuming that more processors automatically make a computation faster.

6637.title: Parallel Clustering
6637.heading: Parallel Clustering
6637.content:
Parallel clustering distributes distance calculations, assignments, or summary updates across several processors or machines. Workers can process different observations while coordinating shared cluster representatives.

Scalability depends on balanced partitions and the size and frequency of exchanged state. Iterative methods may become communication-bound when each round performs little local computation.

6646.title: Parallax as a 3D Matchmove Cue
6646.heading: Parallax as a 3D Matchmove Cue
6646.content: An image-space track can be sufficient when a flat replacement follows a surface without substantial depth change. If the camera moves around an object and reveals formerly hidden sides, nearby and distant features move differently: this parallax exposes a flat-card solution. A 3D camera solve places the replacement at the correct depth and lets its perspective change with the filmed camera. The distinction helps choose between [[Four-Point Corner Pin Tracking]] and [[3D Camera Solve from Feature Tracks]].

6649.title: Parabolic Trough Solar Power Plant
6649.heading: Parabolic Trough Solar Power Plant
6649.content: A parabolic-trough plant connects many [[Parabolic Trough Solar Collector]] modules that heat a circulating fluid along their receiver tubes. Hot oil can be stored and used in a boiler to raise steam for a turbine, then returned cool to the collector field. The source also describes direct steam generation and a backup-fired boiler. Temperature limits of the primary fluid shape operating conditions.

6652.title: Parabolic Trough Solar Collector
6652.heading: Parabolic Trough Solar Collector
6652.content: A parabolic trough is a line-focus [[Concentrating Solar Collector]]. Its curved mirror directs sunlight onto a receiver tube running along the focal line, where flowing fluid gains heat. The trough follows the Sun about one axis. Many trough modules can send their heated fluid to a [[Parabolic Trough Solar Power Plant]]; the individual collector's aperture, tracking, and receiver losses set the heat delivered.

6655.title: Pairwise Social Bot Detection
6655.heading: Pairwise Social Bot Detection
6655.content:
Pairwise social bot detection analyzes relationships between two accounts, such as similarity, interaction, or synchronized behavior. The pair becomes the unit of representation instead of an isolated user.

Pairwise evidence can reveal coordinated automation that individual profiles conceal. The number of possible pairs is large, so candidate generation and meaningful relationship definitions are essential.
